findings.title: Scope the stricter-grading claim to multipart readiness items
findings.problem: The new headline makes an unqualified platform-wide comparison with NCLEX grading. The existing explanation supports a narrower claim: readiness self-assessments require every part of a multipart item to be correct, whereas NCLEX can award partial credit. That does not establish that ordinary practice or all PulseRN grading is stricter. I could not verify ordinary-practice scoring from the supplied files; the new tests only assert that the slogan is reproduced.
findings.failure_scenario: A learner sees this headline while signing up for the free pass, which explicitly excludes readiness self-assessments, and interprets their practice scores as being earned under stricter-than-NCLEX grading. The displayed claim provides no restriction to the readiness scoring behavior actually described.
findings.fix: Qualify the shared headline with the supported behavior, such as "Our readiness self-assessments use all-or-nothing scoring for multipart items," and explain the NCLEX partial-credit distinction. Update the hard-coded index.html fallback and slogan assertions to match.

assessment: One claims issue needs correction. The rendering and page-generation changes otherwise appear consistent. The supplied files do not establish the platform-wide grading comparison introduced by the new slogan.
